Rashi on Pesachim 90b:10:1.hebrew: סבר לה כרבי יצחק דאמר - בספרי, אותן אנשים שבפסח מדבר שהיו טמאין לנפש אדם, טמאי מת מצוה היו, שחל שביעי כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 90b:10:1.english: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Yitzchak, who said - In Sifrei: those people at the wilderness Passover who were ritually impure from a human corpse were impure from a met mitzvah [a corpse with no one to bury it], whose seventh [day] fell, etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:11:1.english: What, is it not that he has not immersed - And [this] is difficult for Rav.

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:12:1.english: It teaches us this, that even though he lacks the setting of the sun, that the sun sets by itself - And he is not like one who lacks an action.

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:13:1.hebrew: הכי נמי מסתברא - דאטבול קאי, מדאצטריך למיתנא סיפא דשוחטין על מחוסר כפורים. אי אמרת בשלמא רישא לא אשמעי' [אלא] טבול יום, איצטריך למיתנא סיפא לאשמעי' דשוחטין על מחוסר כפורים — ס"ד אמינא האי מחוסר מעשה חשיב ליה, קא משמע לן דשרי. ובמסרו לב"ד של כהנים, כדאמרן:
Rashi on Pesachim 90b:13:1.english: So too, it is reasonable - [That is,] it refers to one who has [already] immersed, since it was necessary for the latter clause to teach that one slaughters [the Paschal lamb] for a mechusar kippurim [one who still lacks his atonement offerings]. Granted, if you say [that] the first clause taught us only [the case of] a tevul yom [one who immersed that day and awaits sunset], [then] it was necessary to teach the latter clause to inform us that one slaughters for a mechusar kippurim — [for] it might have entered my mind to say [that] this one is considered lacking an act, [so] it informs us that it is permitted. And [this applies specifically] when he has handed them [his birds] over to the court of priests, as we stated [above].

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:13:2.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת כו' יש בידו לתקן - לטבול, אבל מחוסר כפרה אין בידו לתקן אלא ביד כהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 90b:13:2.english: Rather, if you say, etc., it is in his power to rectify [it] - [i.e.,] to immerse; however, one who lacks atonement does not have it in his power to rectify [it], rather [it is] in the hand of a priest.

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:1:1.hebrew: ואין שוחטין וזורקין על טמא שרץ - ואע"פ שבידו לטבול היום, וטעמא מפרש לקמיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 90b:1:1.english: And one does not slaughter and sprinkle on behalf of one who is impure [due to] a creeping animal - Even though it is in his power to immerse today, and [the Gemara] explains the reason later.

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:20:1.hebrew: זבה טבילתה ביום שביעי - דכתיב (ויקרא ט״ו:כ״ח) "וספרה לה שבעת ימים ואחר תטהר" — אחר מעשה תטהר, כיון דסיימה לה ספירה תטהר, ובתחלת היום עבדה לה ספירה. אבל נדה דאורייתא, שאינה סופרת נקיים אלא שבעה עם ימי ראייתה, אינה טובלת עד לאחר שקיעת החמה של שביעי, והערב שמש בדידה לא הוי עד למחר:
Rashi on Pesachim 90b:20:1.english: A zava's immersion is on the seventh day - As it is written (Leviticus 15:28): "And she shall count for herself seven days, and afterward she shall be pure" — [meaning] after the act [of counting] she becomes pure; once she has completed her counting she becomes pure, and she performs her counting at the beginning of the [seventh] day. However, a niddah by biblical law — who does not count clean [days], but rather seven [days] including the days of her sighting — does not immerse until after sunset of the seventh [day], and the sunset [purification] in her case does not occur until the next day.

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:25:1.english: On the seventh [day], no - Because she is not fit [to eat] in the evening due to [the requirement of] waiting until sunset.

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:26:1.english: She shall be - [The baraita] expounds [the] superfluous [word].

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:26:2.english: And a woman after childbirth is compared to a menstruating woman - For it is written (Leviticus 12), "As in the days of her menstrual flow shall she be unclean."

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:27:1.hebrew: האונן - שמתו מוטל לפניו, כדאמרי' בשחיטת קדשים בפרק טבול יום (זבחים דף ק:): איזהו אונן? כל זמן שלא נקבר:
Rashi on Pesachim 90b:27:1.english: The acute mourner - [One] whose dead [relative] lies before him, as we say in Shechitat Kodashim [Zevachim], in the chapter [entitled] Tevul Yom (Zevachim 100b): "Who is an acute mourner? As long as [the deceased] has not been buried."

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:5:1.english: Those lacking atonement - A zav, a zavah, a metzora'at, and a woman after childbirth.

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:5:2.english: He will be neglectful - and will not immerse.

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:6:2.hebrew: שבשופרות - שופר היה שם שכתוב עליו קינין, ואשה שיש עליה לידה וכן כל מחוסרי כפרה מביאין מעות ונותנין לתוכו. ודמי הקינין קצובין היו, ואוכלים בקדש לערב, וסומכין על חזקת בית דין של כהנים שאין עומדין משם עד שיכלו כל מעות אותו שופר, כדי שלא יאכלו מחוסרי כפרה בקדשים:
Rashi on Pesachim 90b:6:2.english: In the collection boxes - There was a collection box there upon which was written "bird-offerings," and a woman who was obligated [to bring a] childbirth [offering], and likewise all who lacked atonement, would bring money and place [it] inside it. And the price of the bird-offerings was fixed, and they would eat of sacrificial [food] in the evening, relying on the presumption regarding the court of priests that they do not leave from there until all the money of that collection box is used up, so that those lacking atonement would not eat of sacrificial [food].

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:7:1.hebrew: ופרכינן ורב דאמר - שמא פשע, אלמא מדאורייתא מיחזא חזי טמא שרץ לשחוט עליו, ומשום דילמא פשע גזרו ביה רבנן:
Rashi on Pesachim 90b:7:1.english: And we ask: And [according to] Rav, who said - lest he be negligent — thus [indicating that] by Torah law, one who is ritually impure [from] a creeping animal is fit to have [the Paschal lamb] slaughtered on his behalf, and [only] because he might be negligent did the Sages decree regarding him.

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:7:2.hebrew: והאמר רב - בכיצד צולין, היו ישראל מחצה טהורין ומחצה טמאין, מטמאים אחד מהן בשרץ להכריע רוב ציבור לטומאה. ואי מדאורייתא חזי, היאך הוא מכריעם לטומאה, דהיינו טמא שרץ דחזי למטבל:
Rashi on Pesachim 90b:7:2.english: And did Rav not say - In [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin: [If] Israel were half pure and half impure, we contaminate one of them with a creeping animal to tip the majority of the community to impurity. And if by Torah law he is fit, how does he tip them to impurity — namely, one impure [from] a creeping animal, who is fit to immerse?

Rashi on Pesachim 90b:9:1.hebrew: וממאי דהכי - דילמא מדכתיב טמא לנפש ולא כתיב טמא שרץ, שמע מינה טמא מת שאינו ראוי לערב קאמר:
Rashi on Pesachim 90b:9:1.english: And from where [do we know] that this is so - Perhaps, since it is written "impure by a corpse" and it is not written "impure by a creeping creature," infer from this [that] it is speaking of one impure from a corpse, who is not fit [to partake] by evening.

Tosafot on Pesachim 90b:20:1.hebrew: בשמיני פשיטא - אמתניתין דקתני זב שוחטים עליו בשמיני, ליכא למיפרך "פשיטא", דמצי למימר דקתני לה אגב רישא — דזב שראה שתי ראיות, ושומרת יום כנגד יום שוחטין עליה, ולא חיישינן שמא תראה ותסתור:
Tosafot on Pesachim 90b:20:1.english: "On the eighth [day] — it is obvious!" - Regarding our Mishnah, which teaches [that for] a zav we slaughter [the Paschal lamb] on his behalf on the eighth [day], one cannot ask, "It is obvious!", because one can say that it teaches it on account of the first clause — that [for] a zav who saw two sightings, and a woman who observes a day against a day [shomeret yom keneged yom], we slaughter [the Paschal lamb] on her behalf, and we are not concerned lest she see [another discharge] and void [her clean day].

Tosafot on Pesachim 90b:27:1.hebrew: האונן - כגון שמת לו מת אחר חצות, שכבר חל עליו חיוב פסח; אבל קודם חצות חל עליו אנינות, כדאמר במי שהיה טמא (לקמן פסחים דף צח.):
Tosafot on Pesachim 90b:27:1.english: An acute mourner [onen] - For example, when a relative of his died after midday, for the obligation of the Paschal offering had already taken effect upon him; whereas before midday, acute mourning [aninut] takes effect upon him, as it states in [the chapter] Mi Shehayah Tamei (below, Pesachim 98a).

Tosafot on Pesachim 90b:2:1.hebrew: מחוסר טבילה - ואף על גב דמחוסר כפרה נמי צריך טבילה, כדתנן בפ' חומר בקודש (חגיגה דף כא.): "האונן ומחוסר כפורים צריכין טבילה לקודש" — אינו אלא מדרבנן, כדמוכח התם. ועוד, דבההיא טבילה לא בעי הערב שמש, ולא שייך התם "דילמא פשע":
Tosafot on Pesachim 90b:2:1.english: He lacks immersion - And even though one who lacks atonement [mechusar kapparah] also requires immersion, as we learned in the Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Chomer Bakodesh (Chagigah 21a): "An onen and one who lacks atonement require immersion for sacrificial food" — [that immersion] is only by rabbinic decree, as is proven there. And furthermore, for that immersion one does not require sunset, and [the concern of] "lest he be negligent" does not apply there.

Tosafot on Pesachim 90b:6:1.hebrew: עד שיכלו כל המעות שבשופר - הקשה ריב"א: הא אי אפשר שלא יהא מעורב בכל קן וקן ממעות שתי נשים, ואפי' למאן דאמר יש ברירה, כי האי גוונא לא שייך למימר, דאנן סהדי שנתערבו. ואי הוה אמרינן שמכל מעות שבשופר קונה קינין יחד מאדם א', הוה אתי שפיר; אבל לישנא דעד שיכלו לא משמע הכי. ונראה לר"י דכל אחת היתה צוררת מעותיה ונותנת בשופר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 90b:6:1.english: "Until all the money in the shofar [collection box] is used up" - Riva asked: Surely it is impossible that in each and every bird-pair [purchased], there not be [coins] mixed together from the money of two women; and even according to the one who says there is retroactive designation [bereirah], in a case such as this it is not applicable to say [so], for it is certain that they became mixed together. And if we were to say that from all the money in the shofar [the priest] purchases [all] the bird-pairs together from one person, it would work out well; however, the wording "until [the money] is used up" does not imply this. And it appears to R"I that each [woman] would wrap up her money and place [it] into the shofar.

Tosafot on Pesachim 90b:8:1.hebrew: מי לא עסקינן שחל שביעי שלו להיות בערב הפסח - ואם תאמר: ואפילו טבל נמי, לא ישחטו עליו מהאי טעמא? וי"ל: "כי יהיה טמא" כתיב, והאי קלישא טומאתיה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 90b:8:1.english: "Are we not dealing with [one] whose seventh [day] occurred on Passover eve" - And if you say: even if he [already] immersed as well, they should not slaughter [the Paschal lamb] on his behalf for this reason! And one can answer: It is written, "[if any man] shall be impure," whereas this one's impurity is lighter.

Tosafot on Pesachim 90b:8:2.hebrew: שחל שביעי שלו - אבל ששי שלו ליכא למימר, מדכתיב: "ולא יכלו לעשות הפסח ביום ההוא" — הא למחר היו יכולים לעשות ולשחוט הן עצמן בלא שליחות, מדלא כתיב: "ולא יכלו לאכול". אי נמי, דייק מ"ביום ההוא" דמיותר, ואי ששי הוא לישתוק מיניה. ואם תאמר: למה אמר להם לדחות לפסח שני? יטבלו בו ביום וישחטו עליהם! ויש לומר: דשמא כן עשו, ובשעה ששאלו לא טבלו עדיין, ואמר להו משה: אם לא תטבלו היום, תדחו לפסח שני:
Tosafot on Pesachim 90b:8:2.english: Whose seventh [day] occurred [on Passover eve] - However, [that it was] his sixth [day] cannot be said, since it is written: "and they could not make the Paschal offering on that day" — [implying that] on the next day they would have been able to make [it] and slaughter [it] themselves without an agent, since it does not write "and they could not eat." Alternatively, [the Gemara] infers [this] from [the words] "on that day," which are superfluous, for if it were [his] sixth [day], [Scripture] should have omitted it. And if you ask: Why did [Moses] tell them to be deferred to the Second Pesach? Let them immerse on that very day and have [others] slaughter [it] on their behalf! One can say: Perhaps they indeed did so, and at the time they asked they had not yet immersed, and Moses said to them: If you do not immerse today, you will be deferred to the Second Pesach.
